theory.intro: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement, and **acceleration** is the rate of change of velocity. Differentiate the displacement $x(t)$ once to get $v = \dot{x}$, and again to get $a = \ddot{x}$.
facts: The dot notation writes velocity as $\dot{x}$ and acceleration as $\ddot{x}$, where each dot means one differentiation with respect to time $t$.
Acceleration is also written $\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}}$, the second derivative of displacement with respect to time.
Common units are metres for $x$, $\text{m/s}$ for $v$ and $\text{m/s}^{2}$ for $a$.
**Initial** values are the values at $t = 0$, found by substituting $t = 0$ into $x$, $v$ or $a$.
A particle is **at rest** when $v = 0$, which is not the same as being at the origin, where $x = 0$.
The **speed** of a particle is $|v|$, so a velocity of $-6\text{ m/s}$ is a speed of $6\text{ m/s}$.
The particle moves in the positive direction when $v > 0$ and in the negative direction when $v < 0$.
steps: Differentiate the displacement $x(t)$ with respect to $t$ to find the velocity $v = \dot{x}$.
Differentiate the velocity with respect to $t$ to find the acceleration $a = \ddot{x}$.
Substitute the required time into $x$, $v$ or $a$ to evaluate it at that instant.
To find when the particle is at rest, set $v = 0$ and solve for $t \ge 0$.

workedExamples.question_text: A particle moves in a straight line with displacement $x(t)=2t^3-6t^2+5t-3$ metres, where $t\ge0$ is measured in seconds. Find its velocity and acceleration functions, its initial displacement, velocity and acceleration, and its velocity and acceleration at $t=2$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Differentiate displacement once for velocity and twice for acceleration.
$\begin{align*}v(t)&=\dot{x}(t)=6t^2-12t+5\\a(t)&=\ddot{x}(t)=12t-12\end{align*}$
Initial values use $t=0$.
$\begin{align*}x(0)&=-3\text{ m}\\v(0)&=5\text{ m/s}\\a(0)&=-12\text{ m/s}^2\end{align*}$
At $t=2$:
$\begin{align*}v(2)&=6(2)^2-12(2)+5\\&=5\text{ m/s}\\a(2)&=12(2)-12\\&=12\text{ m/s}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has displacement $x(t)=2\cos 4t$ metres, where $t\ge0$ is measured in seconds. Find its velocity and acceleration functions, then evaluate both at $t=\pi/8$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the chain rule at each differentiation.
$\begin{align*}v(t)&=\dot{x}(t)=-8\sin 4t\\a(t)&=\ddot{x}(t)=-32\cos 4t\end{align*}$
At $t=\pi/8$, the angle is $4t=\pi/2$.
$\begin{align*}v(\pi/8)&=-8\sin(\pi/2)\\&=-8\text{ m/s}\\a(\pi/8)&=-32\cos(\pi/2)\\&=0\text{ m/s}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has displacement $x(t)=t^2e^{-2t}$ metres, where $t\ge0$ is measured in seconds. Find its velocity and acceleration as functions of time.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Apply the product rule, using $\dfrac{d}{dt}e^{-2t}=-2e^{-2t}$.
$\begin{align*}v(t)&=2te^{-2t}-2t^2e^{-2t}\\&=(2t-2t^2)e^{-2t}\end{align*}$
Differentiate the velocity using the product rule again.
$\begin{align*}a(t)&=(2-4t)e^{-2t}-2(2t-2t^2)e^{-2t}\\&=(4t^2-8t+2)e^{-2t}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has displacement $x(t)=1+4\ln(t+2)$ metres, where $t\ge0$ is measured in seconds. Find its initial velocity and initial acceleration.
A particle moves in a straight line with displacement $x(t)=t^3-9t^2+15t+2$ metres for $t\ge0$, with $t$ in seconds. Find every time it is at rest and its acceleration at each of those times.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}v(t)&=3t^2-18t+15\\a(t)&=6t-18\end{align*}$
At rest, $v(t)=0$.
$\begin{align*}3t^2-18t+15&=0\\3(t-1)(t-5)&=0\end{align*}$
Both times satisfy $t\ge0$: $t=1\text{ s}$ and $t=5\text{ s}$.
$\begin{align*}a(1)&=6(1)-18\\&=-12\text{ m/s}^2\\a(5)&=6(5)-18\\&=12\text{ m/s}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has displacement $x(t)=3\sin 3t$ metres for $0\le t\le2\pi/3$, with $t$ in seconds. Find every time the particle is at rest.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$v(t)=9\cos 3t$.
At rest, $v(t)=0$, so $\cos 3t=0$. The time restriction gives $0\le3t\le2\pi$.
$\begin{align*}3t&=\frac{\pi}{2}\quad\text{or}\quad\frac{3\pi}{2}\\t&=\frac{\pi}{6}\quad\text{or}\quad\frac{\pi}{2}\end{align*}$
The particle is at rest at $t=\pi/6\text{ s}$ and $t=\pi/2\text{ s}$.

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has displacement $x(t)=t^3-6t^2+7t+4$ metres for $t\ge0$, with $t$ in seconds. Find its velocity when its acceleration is $6\text{ m/s}^2$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}v(t)&=3t^2-12t+7\\a(t)&=6t-12\end{align*}$
Find the time when $a(t)=6$.
$\begin{align*}6t-12&=6\\6t&=18\\t&=3\end{align*}$
Substitute this time into velocity.
$\begin{align*}v(3)&=3(3)^2-12(3)+7\\&=27-36+7\\&=-2\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has displacement $x(t)=t^3-6t^2-15t+8$ metres for $t\ge0$, with $t$ in seconds. Find its displacement at the instant it is at rest.
A particle has displacement $x(t)=t+\dfrac{9}{t+1}$ metres for $t\ge0$, with $t$ in seconds. Find its acceleration at the instant it is at rest.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Write the reciprocal term as $9(t+1)^{-1}$ before differentiating.
$\begin{align*}v(t)&=1-9(t+1)^{-2}\\a(t)&=18(t+1)^{-3}\end{align*}$
At rest, $v(t)=0$.
$\begin{align*}1-\frac{9}{(t+1)^2}&=0\\(t+1)^2&=9\end{align*}$
Since $t\ge0$, $t+1$ is positive. Thus $t+1=3$ and $t=2\text{ s}$.
$\begin{align*}a(2)&=\frac{18}{3^3}\\&=\frac{2}{3}\text{ m/s}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text:
For each displacement function, differentiate twice and show the stated relationship. Displacement is in metres and $t\ge0$ is in seconds.
(a) $x(t)=4\cos 3t$: show that $\ddot{x}=-9x$.
(b) $x(t)=2e^{-3t}$: show that $\ddot{x}=9x$.

development.question_text:
A particle moves in a straight line with $x = 2t^{3} - 9t^{2} + 12t$ metres for $t \ge 0$.
Find the times at which the particle is at rest.

A particle moves in a straight line with $x = t^{3} - 12t + 5$ metres for $t \ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is at rest.

A particle moves with $x = \sin 2t$ metres for $0 \le t \le \pi$ seconds.
Find the times at which the particle is at rest.
development.solution_text:
$v = \dot{x} = 2\cos 2t$
$\text{At rest, } v = 0:$
$\cos 2t = 0$
$\text{For } 0 \le 2t \le 2\pi:\ 2t = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$
$t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ s and } t = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\text{ s}$
